title: Signs Someone Likes You Over Text (and Signs They Don't) — cv.cm
description: Signs someone likes you over text: who starts chats, what reply time really means, questions, voice notes and late chats, with confidence levels.
h1: How can you tell if someone likes you over text?
answer: Over text, interest shows as effort: they start conversations, ask questions back, remember details, write replies about as long as yours, and want to move to a call or a meeting. Reply speed alone means little. Low interest looks like short answers, no questions, and plans that never happen. Judge the pattern over weeks.

sections.h: Why text is easy to misread
body: Messages feel clear when you write them and unclear when you read them. A well-known study on email found that people are much more confident that their tone (such as sarcasm or seriousness) will come across than it really does. The writer hears their own voice; the reader only sees words. The same is true for "haha", "ok" and a single emoji.

So do not decide from one message. Look for steady patterns that do not depend on tone: who starts, who asks, who follows up, and whether chat leads to real time together. These work across chat apps, from WhatsApp and Instagram DMs to WeChat, LINE, KakaoTalk and Zalo.

One more research hint: in a study of speed dates and instant messages, pairs whose writing styles matched each other were more likely to want to meet again and to stay together. When two people are in tune, their messages often start to sound alike: similar length, similar jokes, similar small words.

sections.h: What reply time really tells you
body: Reply speed is the most watched sign and one of the weakest. People reply slowly because they are at work, in class, driving, with family, or because they prefer to reply when they have time to think. Some people turn off notifications. Others reply fast to everyone.

Research on couples also suggests that reply habits follow personality. In one study of students in relationships, people with more anxious attachment tended to reply faster than their partners, and people with more avoidant attachment tended to reply more slowly. A slow reply can be a habit, not a message about you.

ul: Change. If someone always replied within hours and now takes days, something shifted. It may be stress, or a drop in interest.
Effort after a delay. "Sorry, crazy day! Okay, so how did the interview go?" is warm, even if it is slow.
Being online but not replying, again and again, for a long time, while the chat with you goes nowhere.

body.note: Do not use read receipts or last-seen times as a scoreboard. They make you anxious and say little about how someone feels.

ul: One-word replies like "ok", "lol" or "nice" to most messages, with nothing added.
They never ask a question back. If you stop asking, the chat stops.
You always start, and they only reply.
Long gaps every time, with no warmth when they return.
They talk about meeting "sometime" but never pick a day.
They only write when they need something, or late at night.

body: If you see most of these, stop putting in more effort than you get back. Send fewer messages and see if they move toward you. If they do not, let it go kindly. See also what girls mean when they say and what guys mean when they say, for common short replies.

sections.h: How to move from chat to meeting
body: Chat can go on for months without going anywhere. If you like each other, moving to a call or a meeting is the best test of all.

ol: Pick up a topic you both like and make it a plan: "You keep talking about that hotpot place. Want to go this Thursday?"
Give a day and a place. Specific plans are easier to say yes to than "we should hang out".
If they cannot make that day, see if they offer another. "Thursday's bad, but Saturday works" is a good sign.
If you met online or on an app, meet in a public place, tell a friend where you will be, and get there and home on your own.
If they say "maybe" and never offer another time, try once more at most. Then let them be the one to suggest.

body: A short call is a good middle step, especially for long distance: "Want to do a quick call tonight? Typing this is taking forever." For more on what to write, see how to text your crush. cv.cm's Does my crush like me test can help you look at the whole picture.

ul: Waiting a fixed time before you reply to look less interested. It turns chat into a game and makes the other person guess too.
Sending many messages in a row when the other person replies little.
Reading screenshots to friends and asking them to decode every word. They see even less tone than you do.
Checking their online status or social media to see who else they talk to.
Saying big things by text that should be said in person, like a long confession at 2 a.m.

body: If you are anxious about every reply, that feeling deserves attention on its own. The attachment styles article explains why some people feel this more than others.

faq.q: Does a fast reply mean they like you?
faq.a: Not on its own. Some people reply fast to everyone, and many who like you reply slowly because they are busy. Look at effort and questions, not seconds.

faq.q: What does it mean if they text you every day?
faq.a: Daily contact usually means you matter to them in some way. Whether it is romantic shows in the content: personal questions, flirting, and wanting to meet.

faq.q: Do heart emojis mean someone likes you?
faq.a: Sometimes, but many people use hearts with friends and family. Look at whether they use them only with you, and whether the rest of the chat is warm too.

faq.q: Should I text first or wait for them?
faq.a: Text first if you want to talk. A healthy chat has both people starting sometimes. If you are always the one who starts after several weeks, slow down and see if they do.

faq.q: Why do they text a lot but never want to meet?
faq.a: They may be shy, busy, enjoying attention without wanting more, or talking to several people. Suggest one specific plan. Their answer will tell you more than more chat.
